identity.title: The Bulge Asymmetries and Dynamical Evolution (BAaDE) SiO Maser Survey at 86 GHz with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report on the first 1,432 sources observed using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), from the Bulge Asymmetries and Dynamical Evolution (BAaDE) survey

targets.name: BAaDE sources (1432 MSX-selected AGB candidates, southern sample)

coordinates.value: per-source RA/Dec in Table 2 (2MASS or MSX positions)

evidence.quote: The VLA cannot observe 9,074 BAaDE sources (32% of the full sample) since they are located at declinations below $-35\degree$.

question.value: Detect 86 GHz SiO masers toward MSX-selected AGB candidates to obtain line-of-sight velocities, and characterize the CS-emitting and SiO-emitting populations and the SiO line properties

evidence.quote: aims to obtain tens of thousands of line-of-sight velocities from SiO masers in Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars in the Milky Way.
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.01180.S
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01289.S
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01077.S

bands.value: Band 3 (86 GHz SiO plus 98 GHz CS)

evidence.quote: The ALMA spectral setup in Band 3 is described in Table [1](#tab_alma_spw_config)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows at 85.65, 86.25, 86.85 and 97.99 GHz; channel width 244.141 kHz

evidence.quote: Each channel has a width of $244.141$ kHz.
The synthesized beam of the spectral window imaged at 86.25 GHz consisting of 3840 channels was approximately $3\ensuremath{''}\times2\ensuremath{''}$.
For the three cycles, an average rms sensitivity of 14 mJy/beam/channel was obtained.
Cycle 3 observations occurred between December 27th, 2015 and January 21st, 2016, and Cycle 5 observations were performed on January 28th, 2018.

provided.value: Infrared colors used for source selection

evidence.quote: All sources were selected from version 2.3 of the MSX point source catalog
if a 2MASS association existed for a BAaDE source, the phase center was shifted to the 2MASS position using the task *fixvis*.

what.value: Literature SiO and OH maser velocities for comparison

evidence.quote: A $4\ensuremath{''}$ search radius was used to search for possible SiO and OH maser associations in the extensive Database of Astronomical Maser Sources
The International Variable Star Index (cite: 2006SASS...25...47W) contains periods for 61 sources with SiO $v$=1 maser emission in our observed ALMA sample.

pipeline_or_manual.value: BAaDE CASA pipeline adapted from the BAaDE VLA pipeline

evidence.quote: The BAaDE ALMA calibration pipeline is based on the VLA calibration pipeline developed for the BAaDE survey

flux_calibrator.value: QSO B1424–41, QSO B1921–293, PKS 1613–586; spectral slope from 91.46 and 103.49 GHz catalog fluxes

evidence.quote: these quasars were used for flux and bandpass calibration.

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: <5% difference from Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 solar system calibration

evidence.quote: differed by less than 5% from flux calibration using resolved solar system objects and the ’Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012’ standard

self_calibration.value: Phase-only self-cal on brightest line channel; applied to all four spws; fails for CS

evidence.quote: the brightest channel with a line detection was subsequently used for phase-only self-calibration.
CASA’s task *tclean* was used with the Högbom clean deconvolver, Briggs weighting, and Briggs robustness parameter 0.5
CASA’s task *tclean* was used with the Högbom clean deconvolver, Briggs weighting, and Briggs robustness parameter 0.5
Briggs robustness parameter 0.5 (equivalent to robust=0.0 in AIPS)

what.value: Calibration pipeline derived from the BAaDE VLA pipeline

evidence.quote: The BAaDE ALMA calibration pipeline is based on the VLA calibration pipeline developed for the BAaDE survey, see L. O. Sjouwerman et al. (2019, in preparation).

inherited.from_reference: L. O. Sjouwerman et al. (2019, in preparation)

what.value: Source selection from MSX region iiia

evidence.quote: All sources were selected from version 2.3 of the MSX point source catalog (cite: 2003yCat.5114....0E) that coincide with MSX color region *iii*a (cite: 10.1088/0004-637X/705/2/1554).

method.value: fixvis to 2MASS positions, then flux/bandpass/phase calibration with CASA pipeline

evidence.quote: The phase center was adjusted before any standard calibration was performed.

validation.value: Flux scale compared with Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012, <5% difference

evidence.quote: differed by less than 5% from flux calibration using resolved solar system objects

method.value: SNR thresholds on spectra at phase center; phase-only self-cal on brightest channel; final spectra

evidence.quote: Single line detections were required to have an SNR above 5$\sigma$. Multiple line detections could be made down to a 4.5$\sigma$ level, if the velocities from each line agreed within 30 km s$^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: Spectral regions above 8x initial rms removed before robust rms

evidence.quote: spectral regions exceeding 8 times the initial rms noise were removed first.

method.value: tclean imaging of fields with continuum or CS emission; match to SIMBAD

evidence.quote: In order to better understand the nature of these sources, and to determine whether the continuum emission may be associated with the BAaDE sources, the fields were imaged.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit color distributions and velocity statistics

method.value: Gaussian fits to [D]-[E] distributions; Wilcoxon signed-rank test of SiO velocity differences; gamma fit to FWZM; Spearman test; Anderson–Darling test

evidence.quote: Fitting the SiO maser and CS emission populations to individual Gaussian probability distributions with the *fitdistr* function
Fitting the SiO maser and CS emission populations to individual Gaussian probability distributions with the *fitdistr* function
we use the *Common Astronomy Software Applications* (cite: 2007ASPC..376..127M) package.
CASA (cite: 2007ASPC..376..127M), *fitdistr* (cite: ISBN0-387-95457-0), MASS (cite: ISBN0-387-95457-0), *mclust* (cite: ISSN2073-4859_doi10.21236/ada459792)

used_for.value: listed in software; specific use not stated

evidence.quote: *mclust* (cite: ISSN2073-4859_doi10.21236/ada459792)
the mean and standard deviations of the SiO emission distribution in $[\textnormal{D}]-[\textnormal{E}]$ are $0.691 \pm 0.013$ and $0.264 \pm 0.009$ magnitudes
$1.84 \pm 0.10$ and $0.70 \pm 0.07$ magnitudes
the detection rate jumps to 80% if limiting source selection to $[\textnormal{D}]-[\textnormal{E}] \le 1.38$

results_numeric.quantity: Velocity range containing 90% of SiO v=1 emission

evidence.quote: for 90% of the sources with SiO $v$=1 emission, the emission is limited to a velocity range of 13 km s$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: Most CS emitters have extended emission and are likely YSOs rather than AGB stars

evidence.quote: The majority of fields show extended CS emission, thus arguing against unresolved carbon-rich stars or compact HII regions dominating the population of CS emitters.

claims.hypothesis: SiO detection rate is high among color-selected oxygen-rich sources
claims.experiment: Pipeline line detection in 1432 ALMA fields
claims.finding: MSX selection efficiently yields SiO masers

evidence.quote: A 71% detection rate of 86 GHz SiO masers is obtained from the infrared color-selected sample

claims.hypothesis: Sources with [D]-[E] > 1.38 are not late-type AGB stars
claims.experiment: Colors, CS imaging, Galactic distribution, l-v

evidence.quote: the population of sources with $[\textnormal{D}]-[\textnormal{E}] > 1.38$ probably consists of young stellar objects, or alternatively, planetary nebulae.

claims.hypothesis: Any SiO transition gives the same stellar velocity
claims.experiment: Wilcoxon test of velocity differences relative to v=1
claims.result: No systematic shift within channel width

evidence.quote: there is no evidence of a systematic red- or blue-shift of any other line-peak velocity with respect to the SiO $v$=1 line, within our channel widths.

why_this_data.value: ALMA reaches the low-declination sources the VLA cannot observe

evidence.quote: Since ALMA cannot observe the 43 GHz frequencies associated with $J$=1–0 SiO maser transitions, the ALMA sample is instead surveyed in the $J$=2–1 rotational transitions at 86 GHz.

limitations_admitted.value: Spectra assume source at phase center; positional errors can cause non-detections; SiO variability makes brightness only indicative

evidence.quote: Especially for weaker sources, a 2$\ensuremath{''}$ positional error could result in a non-detection in the pipeline.

referee_caveats_inferred: Far-IR confusion and variability limit the interpretation of detection rates
Single-epoch SiO observations; no distances for CS emitters

data_public_as_stated.value: Spectra on BAaDE website; project codes given; machine-readable tables

evidence.quote: A complete list of spectra are available at the BAaDE survey’s website www.phys.unm.edu/$\sim$baade.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several hundred GB to ~1 TB raw for ~1400 short pointings across three projects
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public with project codes and stated thresholds, but pipeline code is unreleased and several settings are unspecified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Pipeline details are unreleased and the recipe is not complete enough to redo.
